newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police detain 70 in anti-extremist protests.
newsitem.headline: German police detain 70 in anti-extremist protests.

text.p: Police said on Sunday they had detained 70 people during protests by leftist militants against right-wing extremism in the east German city of Magdeburg.
Twenty-five people were arrested after around 400 protesters, some masked, threw bottles and stones at police during a march on Saturday.

The march was organised in response to the killing of a 17-year-old punk rocker who was beaten and stabbed to death earlier this month. An extreme right-winger has been arrested on suspicion of carrying out the attack.

A further 45 people were detained on Saturday night when a group of "punks", a term often used in Germany to describe militants, tried to barricade themselves into a street and then fled to an empty house. Police stormed the house.
A police spokesman said 22 officers had been injured in Saturday's operations. There were no figures for the number of injured demonstrators.
